findings.chapter: Chapter 4: The Anatomy of an AI Workload
findings.evidence: Figure 4.1 caption reads: '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual] ... drawn for clarity: it draws one representative influence per dimension and does not enumerate every influence it asserts (the latency SLO also shapes serving configuration; the token profile also drives KV sizing and prefill demand).' The image provided (rendered page 81) shows arrows from Dimensions to Decisions. Looking closely at the text labels inside the diagram boxes in Figure 4.1: 'Quality requirements → model size/type'; 'Request rate & arrival pattern → concurrency & batching'; etc. The defect is that the caption critiques the figure ('draws one representative influence') but the figure itself contains no visual indicator of this limitation (like dotted lines for secondary influences). This is a minor prose/figure mismatch but arguably acceptable. A stronger defect is on Page 79 in the sidebar table 'Per 1K req' column. For 'Cloud, 6 hosts — 730-hour paid-occupancy input', the value is '≈ $14.04 †'. For 'Self-host — 21-host peak KV-screen fleet', the value is '≈ $24.97 *'. The footnote † explains the hour-basis artifact. The asterisk * explains 'Peak-provisioned capacity ÷ average... volume'. The inconsistency is that row 1 (average fleet) uses a 730h basis for cost but active-hours volume for denominator? No, footnote says '730-hour spend over an active-hours volume'. Row 3 (self-host peak) uses 730h energy calendar. These bases are mixed across rows. Some use active hours, some use wall-clock. The table lacks a unified 'Basis' column, relying on footnotes scattered after the table. This makes comparison impossible without jumping back and forth.
findings.issue: Poor Data Presentation / Unit Consistency: The cost-per-1K-request table on Page 79 compares figures calculated on three different time bases (active-hours matched, wall-clock paid-occupancy, self-host energy-calculated). While footnotes explain the mismatches, presenting them in a single comparative column without explicit base labeling creates a high cognitive load and risk of misinterpretation by readers who might assume they are directly comparable unit costs.
findings.fix_instruction: Restructure the table to include a 'Time Basis' column or separate the rows into two distinct tables: 'Active-Hours Matched Costs' and 'Wall-Clock Provisioned Costs', rather than mixing them in one list with dense footnotes.
